result:
Good. Next is how someone stops the repeating alert. This choice changes what we build more than anything else left.

My proposal is that the on-call person replies "OK" to the text. That is easy at 3 a.m. with cold hands. But the text service must then reach your service from the internet to deliver the reply. Today `ingest/` only talks to your local broker, so this adds a public entry point.

The other options are a link in the text or a button on a local page. Both have their own cost. A link also needs to be reachable from outside. A local page means the person must be on the greenhouse network, or connected to it.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Sending a text needs only an outbound connection to the text service. Receiving a reply needs that service to call into your network. That is the main step up in exposure.
- The current design keeps everything inside: sensors post to MQTT, `ingest/` writes to `greenhouse.db`. The choice here decides whether that stays true.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

When the person on call gets the alert, where will they be, and how do you picture them telling the system "I've got it"?
